title: U.S. House · Pennsylvania's 14th Congressional District
area: Southwestern Pennsylvania, including Washington, Greene, Fayette, and parts of Allegheny and Westmoreland counties.

context.text: Incumbent Republican Guy Reschenthaler and Democrat Alan Bradstock each advanced from their May 19, 2026 primaries.

summary.text: Guy Reschenthaler is the incumbent Republican U.S. Representative for Pennsylvania's 14th District, serving since January 2019. A former Navy Judge Advocate General (JAG) Corps attorney who deployed to Iraq, he later served as a magisterial district judge and a Pennsylvania state senator before winning his House seat. In the 119th Congress he is House Republican Chief Deputy Whip and a member of the Appropriations Committee.

background.text: Born in Pittsburgh in 1983; his House website says he is the son of former teachers and was raised in southwestern Pennsylvania.
Graduated from Penn State, The Behrend College (B.A., 2004, per Wikipedia) and from Duquesne University School of Law (J.D., 2007, per Wikipedia).

Joined the U.S. Navy Judge Advocate General's Corps after law school and volunteered for duty in Iraq. According to his House website, he prosecuted nearly 100 terrorists in Baghdad, defended a Navy SEAL in a case related to the capture of the "Butcher of Fallujah," and later served as Officer in Charge of the Naval Legal Service Office for Texas and Oklahoma.
Returned to southwestern Pennsylvania, where he practiced law and, per his House website, was a partner in a real estate brokerage and related businesses employing roughly a dozen people.
Elected Magisterial District Judge in 2013, winning the nomination of both parties, and served in that role from 2013 to 2015.
Elected to the Pennsylvania State Senate in 2015 to represent the 37th District (parts of Allegheny and Washington counties), serving until 2019.

Elected to the U.S. House in 2018 and sworn in for a fourth term on January 3, 2025. His House website says he serves as House Chief Deputy Whip and on the Appropriations Committee, including its Energy and Water Development, Interior and Environment, and National Security, Department of State subcommittees.
Became House Republican Chief Deputy Whip in January 2023; in the 118th Congress (2023–2024) he also sat on Appropriations, per Ballotpedia.

positions.summary: Voted no on the Bipartisan Background Checks Act of 2019, which would have required background checks on private firearm transfers.

In May 2023 praised House passage of H.R. 2, the Secure the Border Act, a package his statement says would, among other things, increase Border Patrol agents, end catch and release and resume border wall construction.
positions.quote: The Secure the Border Act is the most comprehensive immigration package passed through a chamber of Congress in modern history.

record.text: Vice Chairman of the House Committee on Rules and member of the House Committee on Appropriations (Energy and Water Development, Interior and Environment, and State-Foreign Operations subcommittees) during the 118th Congress, 2023–2024.
In the 119th Congress (2025–2026), serves as House Chief Deputy Whip and a member of the House Appropriations Committee.
Voted no on the Bipartisan Background Checks Act of 2019 (H.R. 8), which passed the House 240–190.
Voted no on the Elijah E. Cummings Lower Drug Costs Now Act (H.R. 3), which passed the House 230–192.
Voted no on the American Dream and Promise Act of 2019 (H.R. 6), which passed the House 237–187.

summary.text: Alan Bradstock is the Democratic nominee for Pennsylvania's 14th District. A Donora native, he describes a career as a U.S. Army aviation officer who deployed during Operation Desert Storm, a 20-year FBI special agent, and later a KPMG auditor, financial adviser and intelligence-community contractor. This is his first run for elected office; his campaign emphasizes economic security, health care, veterans and limiting money in politics.

background.text: Native of Donora, Pennsylvania, and a graduate of Ringgold High School in Washington County, according to his campaign website.

Earned a bachelor's degree in accounting from Washington & Jefferson College, graduating cum laude and Phi Beta Kappa, and played four years of basketball there; he was recently inducted into the college's Athletics Hall of Fame.

Commissioned as a U.S. Army aviation officer after college, serving eight years; his campaign says he was stationed in Germany during the fall of the Berlin Wall, deployed to the Middle East during Operation Desert Storm and earned a master's degree in international relations through Troy State University's overseas program.

Spent two decades as an FBI special agent: after New Agent Training at Quantico he worked drug, public-corruption, kidnapping and violent-crime cases in Las Cruces, New Mexico, then became a Counterterrorism Division supervisor with assignments at CIA Headquarters and the DEA's Special Operations Division, and later served in Louisville, Kentucky.
Served as Deputy Legal Attaché at the U.S. Embassy in Ottawa, working with Canadian law enforcement and intelligence agencies.
In the private sector, worked as an auditor for KPMG, as an independent financial adviser, and as a contractor supporting the U.S. Intelligence Community in budget, strategy and program management.
Announced his candidacy in November 2025; WESA reported it is his first run for elected office. He was unopposed in the May 19, 2026 Democratic primary (48,774 votes).
Lives in Fayette County with his wife and has two children, according to his campaign website.

priorities.text: Calls for policies that raise wages, strengthen workers' rights, and expand opportunities for small businesses so economic growth benefits working families rather than just the wealthy.
Says no one should go bankrupt because they got sick, citing rising premiums and medical debt as reasons to expand access to affordable health care.
priorities.quote: In the richest country on earth, no one should go bankrupt just because they got sick.

priorities.text: Calls for stronger campaign finance laws, greater transparency in political donations, and limits on dark money to reduce the influence of wealthy donors and corporate lobbyists.

positions.summary: His campaign site calls for a universal system covering every American and says health care should be guaranteed as a right.
positions.quote: It's time to guarantee health care as a right, not a privilege. A universal system would cover every American, lower out-of-pocket costs, and make prescriptions and emergency care affordable.

statements.quote: reforming the tax code so it rewards work rather than just wealth
statements.context: On his campaign website's Economic Security issue page
